import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useMemo, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { LOCALE_COOKIE, LOCALE_PARAM, type Locale } from "./config";
import { MESSAGES, type Messages } from "./messages";

interface I18nState {
  locale: Locale;
  setLocale: (next: Locale) => void;
}

const Ctx = createContext<I18nState | null>(null);

/** Holds the page language. The server picks the first one, so the page never flashes English. */
export function I18nProvider({ initialLocale, children }: { initialLocale: Locale; children: ReactNode }) {
  const [locale, setLocaleState] = useState<Locale>(initialLocale);

  const setLocale = useCallback((next: Locale) => {
    setLocaleState(next);
    document.documentElement.lang = next;
    document.cookie = `${LOCALE_COOKIE}=${next}; path=/; max-age=${60 * 60 * 24 * 365}; samesite=lax`;
    // A ?lang= in the address would override the new choice on reload, so drop it.
    const url = new URL(window.location.href);
    if (url.searchParams.has(LOCALE_PARAM)) {
      url.searchParams.delete(LOCALE_PARAM);
      window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", url);
    }
  }, []);

  const value = useMemo(() => ({ locale, setLocale }), [locale, setLocale]);
  return <Ctx.Provider value={value}>{children}</Ctx.Provider>;
}

export function useLocale(): I18nState {
  const v = useContext(Ctx);
  if (!v) throw new Error("useLocale must be used inside <I18nProvider>");

I've translated the watch page and the shared transcript and settings components into all six languages. Both `tsc` runs (web and extension) pass with no errors, and `npm test` passes (39 passed, 2 skipped). I haven't looked at it in a browser: I didn't start the dev server.

**Files changed or added**
- `packages/shared/src/react/labels.ts` (new): the label types and English defaults. It's exported from `packages/shared/src/react/index.ts`.
- `packages/shared/src/react/StatusBadge.tsx`, `TranscriptView.tsx`, `TranscriptToolbar.tsx`, `CaptionSettingsForm.tsx`, `LanguageSettings.tsx`: each takes the new `labels` prop.
- `apps/web/src/app/watch/WatchExperience.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/watch/WatchShell.tsx`, `apps/web/src/components/StartGuide.tsx`, `apps/web/src/components/SettingsPopover.tsx`
- `apps/web/src/components/useSharedLabels.ts` (new): a hook that returns `useT("watch").ui` and, for languages other than English, adds language names from `Intl.DisplayNames`. I put it in its own file because `SettingsPopover` importing from `WatchExperience` would have been a circular import.
- `apps/web/src/i18n/messages/{en,es,fr,pt,de,ja}/watch.ts`: filled in, with sections `shell`, `player`, `hints`, `banners`, `transcript`, `playerError`, `settings`, `guide` (with `steps[3]`) and `ui` (typed as `SharedUiLabels`).

**Labels prop API**
Every component takes an optional `labels?: Partial<X>`. Anything missing falls back to `DEFAULT_*_LABELS`, which match today's English exactly, so the extension needs no changes.
- `StatusBadge`: `StatusBadgeLabels { status: Record<TranscriptionStatus,string>; aria(label) }`. `STATUS_LABELS` is still exported and holds the same English values.
- `TranscriptView`: `TranscriptViewLabels { region, empty, noMatches(q), jumpTo(ts), jumpToLive, jumpToLatest }`
- `TranscriptToolbar`: `TranscriptToolbarLabels { search, clearSearch, copy, download, formats: { txt|srt|vtt: [label, hint] } }`
- `CaptionSettingsForm`: `CaptionSettingsLabels { showCaptions, textSize, sizes[6], background, backgrounds{solid,translucent,none}, opacity, text, textColor(c), fonts{sans,serif,mono}, lines, placement, overVideo, belowVideo, reset, language? }`. The `language` part is passed on to `LanguageSettings`.
- `LanguageSettings` and `TranslationNotice`: `LanguageSettingsLabels` (all the translation status messages, `pair(from, to)`, and an optional `languageName(code)` override).
- `SharedUiLabels` bundles all of these into one object.

**Other changes**
- `<LanguagePicker className="ml-auto shrink-0" />` is now at the right end of the watch page header, after the URL form.
- `StartGuide` takes its step titles and bodies from `t.steps[i]` and still uses the `Art` components from `CAPTURE_STEPS`. `StepArt.tsx` is unchanged.

**Left in English, and why**
- Captions, transcript text, video titles, timestamps, the download file name and exported file contents, as you asked.
- The keyboard hints "(c)" and "(f)", because those are the actual keys.
- Font names "Sans/Serif/Mono" in every language except Japanese (ゴシック, 明朝, 等幅).
- Size letters XS through 2XL, except Portuguese, which uses PP, P, M, G, GG, XG.
- Error text that comes from somewhere else (`support.reason`, capture errors, player error messages, Deepgram session errors) is still English. Only the "Captions stopped:" prefix around it is translated. Those strings are built in `lib/capture`, the player code and the shared session code, and translating them would mean changes there.
- The language names in the extension are still English. On the web they're shown in the page language through `Intl.DisplayNames`, falling back to English in browsers without it.

The automatic-language check in `WatchExperience` still matches the English wording of session errors with `/API key/` and `/doesn.t provide.../`. I didn't change that, since those error strings themselves aren't translated.
